Based on the elements you mentioned—people forming a pile of bodies, traversing the afterlife, and an upside-down structural twist—you might be thinking of a few different things: 
  1. As Above, So Below (2014): In this subterranean horror film, urban explorers travel down through the Paris Catacombs, which turn out to be a literal manifestation of Dante’s circles of Hell. To escape, they must confront their sins and jump down into a bottomless pit, only to find that down is up—they pop open a manhole cover and climb out onto the normal streets of Paris. Piles of human bones and contorted figures feature heavily throughout their descent. 
  2. What Dreams May Come (1998): This film features a visually striking depiction of Hell where the damned are packed together, forming a literal floor and massive, writhing hills of agonizing bodies that the protagonist has to walk over to rescue his wife. 
  3. Dante's Inferno: In the classic text, Dante and Virgil escape Hell by climbing down the fur of a giant, trapped Lucifer at the center of the Earth. Once they pass his midpoint, gravity flips completely upside-down, meaning they must climb "up" through the center to reach the mountain of Purgatory on the other side of the world.
